waveName: Wave 3 – Mosaic colour quality, live preview, freeform, face guidance, viewer features, PDF foundations, portability

package.title: Reliable freeform validation and a usable contour editor
package.goal: Freeform stones can no longer overlap or silently lose their joint. Errors are explained in the user's language and point to the affected piece. Drawing a custom cut stone is practical on desktop and touch.
steps:
geometry.ts:
- triangulate(poly): ear clipping on the cleaned polygon, made CCW first.
- polygonIntersectionArea(a,b): sum over triangle pairs, clipping each by the other's half-planes with clipHalfPlane.
- polygonDistance(a,b): 0 when edges intersect (including collinear or touching) or a vertex lies inside the other polygon; otherwise the minimum vertex-to-segment distance.

edits.ts validateFreePieces(cellW, cellH, pieces, minPieceMm, joint):
- Return typed issues: noPieces, tooMany{max}, tooFewPoints{piece}, selfIntersect{piece}, outside{piece}, areaTooSmall{piece}, overlap{a,b} when the intersection area is > 0.01 mm², thin{piece,minMm}.
- When joint > 0 and the gap is < joint - 0.01 mm, add a gap{a,b,gapMm} WARNING (not an error).
- setFreePieces passes layout.joint.
pieces.ts: add freePreset(kind, w, h, joint) for full, diagonal ╲, diagonal ╱, half, rhombus and trapezoid. Build them on diagA, diagB, lineSplit and subRects so they include the joint.

FreeformEditor:
- SVG viewBox in mm, width min(560px, 100%), max-height 60vh. Convert pointer positions with getScreenCTM().inverse().
- Draggable vertices: setPointerCapture, touch-action:none, snap to cell edges within 0.2 mm, no extra point added after a drag.
- Click an edge midpoint to insert a vertex; each vertex row has a delete control.
- 'Neu zeichnen' button and preset buttons.
- Stop rounding the pre-filled pieces; round only clicked or dragged points to 0.1 mm.
- Live edge lengths, a dashed closing segment, and the active piece's area.
- Pieces with issues get a red dashed outline. Issues are translated, one per line, e.g. 'Teil 1 und Teil 3 überlappen sich'. A reason is shown next to the disabled Speichern button.

StoneDialog:
- Show a badge 'Material fehlt (gelöscht oder nicht importiert)' instead of '?'.
- Use paletteDisplayName for colour names.
- Override edit.lineHint with explicit directions: 0° = senkrecht, 45° = ╱, 90° = waagerecht, 135° = ╲, offset in mm.
acceptance: Unit tests: two 8×5 strips overlapping in an 8×8 cell are rejected. The stacked pair [[3.5,4],[5.5,4],[5.5,7.5],[3.5,7.5]] / [[3.5,1.5],[5.5,1.5],[5.5,5.5],[3.5,5.5]] is rejected. Two triangles sharing a diagonal with a 1 mm gap are accepted. Touching pieces give a gap warning, not an error.
Round trip: every DIAG, SUB and LINE cell opened in the editor validates with no errors and no gap warnings, across 6 tile sizes and joints of 0.5-3 mm. Every freePreset validates.
e2e: on a diagonal cell, 'Neu zeichnen', draw a triangle, drag one vertex (its table coordinates change), save. The stone count and cut template reflect the new piece.
package.risk: Effort M-L. Gap is a warning so that existing saved projects still open. Keep the exact cut dimensions coming from analyzeCut.

findings.title: Freeform validation accepts overlapping stones and stones with no joint; joint area can go negative
findings.problem: validateFreePieces relies on polygonsOverlap, which only detects strictly crossing edges (segIntersect excludes collinear and endpoint contacts) plus a centroid-in-polygon test. Overlaps where edges are collinear or vertices lie on edges are missed, which is typical when drawing on the editor's 0.1 mm grid. The function also never checks that pieces are at least one joint apart, so stones can touch. The overlap is then counted twice: stoneArea becomes larger than the finished area and jointArea goes negative. The invariant 'Steinfläche + Fugenfläche = Gesamtfläche' cannot catch this because stats.ts defines jointArea = finishedArea - stoneArea, so it holds by construction.
findings.evidence: src/core/geometry.ts:159-165 (strict t/u bounds), :191-201 (centroid test); src/core/edits.ts:87-107 (no gap check); src/core/stats.ts:223. Random search /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/correctness-core/t5_overlap_search.ts: 236 of 71,158 overlapping rect/triangle pairs (>0.25 mm² shared) are NOT detected, e.g. A=[[3.5,4],[5.5,4],[5.5,7.5],[3.5,7.5]] B=[[3.5,1.5],[5.5,1.5],[5.5,5.5],[3.5,5.5]] overlap 3 mm². r4_free_validation.out: 'E2: two 8x5 rects overlapping 8x2 in an 8x8 cell: setFreePieces ok=true; ... stoneArea=144 jointArea=-16 (finished area 128)'; 'C: touching, 0 mm gap (joint is 1 mm): ok=true'. tests/core.test.ts:261 asserts only the tautology.
findings.proposal: In validateFreePieces: (1) Compute the exact overlap area by ear-clipping each polygon into triangles and summing the convex intersections with clipHalfPlane (pieces may be non-convex); error 'overlap' if the area exceeds 1e-4 mm². (2) Add a `joint` parameter and error 'gap' when the minimum segment-to-segment distance between two pieces is below joint - 0.01 mm (see polyDist in the scratch lib.ts). Pass layout.joint from setFreePieces and FreeformEditor. In computeStats, also sum the cell areas and flag an error when stoneArea > sum of cell areas. Change tests/core.test.ts:261 to compare jointArea with an independently computed value: finished area - sum of cell areas + sum of (cell area - piece area) per cell.
corrected:
1) src/core/geometry.ts: add triangulate(poly) (ear clipping on a cleanPoly'd simple polygon; make it counter-clockwise first by reversing when signedArea<0) and overlapArea(a,b). overlapArea sums, over every pair of triangles, the area left after clipping triangle A with clipHalfPlane against each edge of triangle B. For a CCW triangle, keep nx*x+ny*y <= c with n = -(left normal) and c = n·p. A working prototype is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/verify-correctness-core-1/v2_fix_proto.ts.

2) src/core/edits.ts validateFreePieces: replace polygonsOverlap with `overlapArea(polys[i], polys[j]) > 1e-3` and push the error `overlap i/j`. Keep the existing i18n text, or add one that shows the overlap in mm². Add an optional `joint` parameter. When joint > 0 and the minimum segment-to-segment distance between two pieces is below joint - 0.01 mm, push a WARNING (not an error) `gap i/j`, so the user can still deliberately use narrower joints in detail areas. Pass layout.joint from setFreePieces and FreeformEditor (StoneDialog.tsx, ~line 326). Add de/en/tr strings for the gap warning showing the actual gap and the joint width.

3) src/core/stats.ts (optional, defensive): while looping, add up each cell's piece area. If it exceeds cell w*h + 1e-6, count the cell in a new `overlapCells` field on the stats result. Show a warning in the material/stats UI when it is above 0, so projects saved before the fix (serialize.ts loads free pieces without validation) are flagged. Do not clamp jointArea, because that would hide the error.

4) tests/core.test.ts: add regression tests that validateFreePieces rejects the 8x5/8x5 strips in an 8x8 cell and the stacked pair [[3.5,4],[5.5,4],[5.5,7.5],[3.5,7.5]] / [[3.5,1.5],[5.5,1.5],[5.5,5.5],[3.5,5.5]]. Also check that it still accepts two triangles sharing a diagonal and a clean split with a 1 mm gap. Replace the tautological check at line 261 with a real invariant: for every cell, the sum of cellPieces areas must be ≤ cellRect area, and every pair of pieces must have overlapArea ≈ 0. Assert stoneArea ≤ the sum of cell areas and jointArea ≥ the finished area minus the sum of cell areas (the area between cells). Do not use the rewritten formula 'finished - Σcell + Σ(cell - piece)': it simplifies to finished - Σpiece and is still a tautology.

1) src/core/geometry.ts:
- Add triangulate(poly), using ear-clipping on the simple, cleaned polygon.
- Add polygonIntersectionArea(a, b): sum, over triangle pairs, the area of each triangle clipped by the other triangle's three edge half-planes with clipHalfPlane. Orient both triangles counter-clockwise first.
- Add polygonDistance(a, b): 0 if the edges intersect, including collinear and endpoint contact, or if a vertex of one polygon lies strictly inside the other. Otherwise the minimum vertex-to-segment distance.
- Keep polygonsOverlap only as a fast pre-check, or replace it.

2) src/core/edits.ts validateFreePieces(cellW, cellH, pieces, minPieceMm, joint):
- Hard error `overlap i/j` when the intersection area is above 0.01 mm². This is well below anything cuttable, and the editor still rejects overlaps such as E1 (3 mm²) and E2 (16 mm²).
- When joint > 0 and polygonDistance < joint - 0.01 mm, add a structured warning {type:'gap', a:i, b:j, gapMm} instead of an error. The editor shows "Fuge zwischen Teil 1 und 2: 0,4 mm (Projektfuge 1 mm)". Touching pieces (gap 0) are still saveable but clearly flagged.
- Pass layout.joint from setFreePieces and from FreeformEditor (StoneDialog.tsx:297 and 326).

3) src/ui/project/StoneDialog.tsx:
- Stop rounding the pre-filled pieces to 0.1 mm at line 321. Keep exact coordinates, or round to 0.01 mm. Snap only newly clicked points to 0.1 mm.
- At line 447, replace v.errors.join with i18n keys (free.err.overlap, free.warn.gap with {a},{b},{gap},{joint}) in de, en and tr.

4) src/core/stats.ts:
- For every FREE cell, re-run the validation; FREE cells are few, so this is cheap. Count invalid cells (overlaps) in a new stats.invalidFreeCells.
- Show a visible warning in StepPlan and on the PDF material page listing those stone IDs. Do not clamp jointArea or otherwise hide a negative value; show the warning instead. This also covers projects already saved in IndexedDB with overlapping free pieces, since serialize.ts does not validate them on load.

5) tests:
- E1 and E2 and the 10x10 halves overlapping by 2 mm are rejected.
- Touching pieces give a gap warning, not an error.
- Round trip: every DIAG, SUB and LINE cell opened in the editor validates with no errors and no gap warnings. Use roundtrip.ts as the template.
- Per-cell invariant: the summed piece area of a cell is at most the cell area + 1e-6, checked over random edits.
- Replace the tautology at tests/core.test.ts:261 with an independent calculation: jointArea = finishedArea - Σcell areas + Σ(cell area - Σpiece areas).

Impact 3, effort M.

findings.title: Raw developer error strings shown to users (freeform 'overlap 1/3', 'self-intersecting'); core errors hard-coded in German
findings.problem: The freeform editor shows English debug codes in red in the German UI, without saying which piece to fix. Core layout and colour errors are thrown as German text and shown verbatim in the EN and TR UIs, so the app's three languages mix.
findings.evidence: shots/j2-08-freeform-points.png shows 'overlap 1/3 · overlap 2/3' under the coordinate table (journey2 log: freeform errors [ 'overlap 1/3 · overlap 2/3' ]). Code: src/core/edits.ts:90-105 pushes 'no-pieces', 'piece n: <3', 'piece n: self-intersecting', 'overlap i/j'; src/ui/project/StoneDialog.tsx:447 renders v.errors.join(' · '). German throws: src/core/layout.ts:59, :68, :126; src/core/color.ts:88, displayed raw by LayoutSummary (src/ui/project/StepGeometry.tsx:12).
findings.proposal: Return structured issues from validateFreePieces: {code:'overlap', a:1, b:3} | {code:'selfIntersect', piece} | {code:'tooFewPoints', piece} | {code:'outside', piece} | {code:'tooSmall', piece}. Translate them with new keys free.err.* (e.g. 'Teil 1 und Teil 3 überlappen sich'), and outline the offending pieces red in the SVG. Do the same for computeLayout errors (layout.err.*) and translate them in LayoutSummary.
corrected:
1) src/core/edits.ts: change FreeValidation to errors: FreeIssue[] and warnings: FreeIssue[], where FreeIssue = {code:'noPieces'} | {code:'tooMany', max:16} | {code:'tooFewPoints', piece} | {code:'selfIntersect', piece} | {code:'outside', piece} | {code:'areaTooSmall', piece, minMm2:0.25} | {code:'overlap', a, b} | {code:'thin', piece, minMm}. Keep every check, the 1e-6 and 0.25 tolerances, and the ok logic byte-for-byte as they are. Only the payload changes.

2) StoneDialog.tsx FreeformEditor: render each issue as t(`free.err.${code}`, params), one per line. Example DE strings: 'Teil 1 und Teil 3 überlappen sich – Punkte verschieben, bis sich die Flächen nicht mehr berühren.', 'Teil 2 kreuzt sich selbst – Punktreihenfolge prüfen.', 'Teil 2 liegt teilweise außerhalb der Zelle ({w} × {h} mm).', 'Teil 4 hat weniger als 3 Punkte.', 'Teil 4 ist kleiner als 0,25 mm².', 'Höchstens 16 Teile pro Zelle.'. Add en and tr versions too. Draw affected pieces with a red dashed stroke in the SVG, add a red dot on their Teil-n tabs, and give the thin warning the piece number. Put a short reason next to the disabled Speichern button, e.g. 'Speichern erst möglich, wenn alle Fehler behoben sind'.

3) src/core/layout.ts: throw class LayoutError extends Error { code: 'invalidDims' | 'smallerThanTile' | 'tooManyCells'; params }. Keep the current German message as e.message so the core stays free of UI dependencies. In useProject.ts:206-211, store {code, params, message}. LayoutSummary (StepGeometry.tsx:12) renders t(`layout.err.${code}`, params) and falls back to message, with locale-formatted numbers via n(). For smallerThanTile, add a hint: 'Projekt mindestens {tile} mm breit/hoch machen oder Randmodus mit Zuschnitt wählen'.

4) Optional, same pattern: give the mosaic.ts:446/466 empty-palette errors and edits.ts:175 (last colour) codes the UI translates through the existing compute.err.* fallback (StepCompute.tsx:80). Leave the 'abgebrochen' cancel signal (client.ts:64, useProject.ts:350) unchanged, or replace both ends together with a dedicated code. Drop color.ts:88 from scope, since users can't reach it.

5) Tests: add unit cases in tests/core.test.ts that check the exact codes and piece numbers for overlap, self-intersection, outside and too-few-points, and that ok/accept results are unchanged for the existing cases. tests/i18n.test.ts will then enforce the new free.err.* and layout.err.* keys in de, en and tr.

findings.title: Freeform contour editor is hard to use (starts pre-filled, tiny canvas, no vertex dragging, no measurements)
findings.problem: 'Freiform …' opens with the cell's existing pieces already present. Clicking adds points to those pieces, which immediately triggers overlap errors; there is no 'start empty'. A 5×5 mm cell is drawn on a fixed 320 px canvas, vertices cannot be dragged (only edited as numbers), and no edge lengths or angles are shown while drawing. A custom cut stone (requirement 5) is therefore hard to make.
findings.evidence: shots/j2-07-freeform.png and shots/j2-08-freeform-points.png: after '+ Neues Teil' and 3 clicks, 'overlap 1/3 · overlap 2/3' and Speichern disabled, because Teil 1/2 (the old triangles) remain. Code: src/ui/project/StoneDialog.tsx:292 (initial = current pieces), :323 (`const size = 320`), :327-337 (onClick only appends points, no drag handlers on the circles).
findings.proposal: In FreeformEditor: add 'Neu zeichnen' (clear all) and shape presets (Dreieck, Trapez, Raute, Rechteck) that generate an editable polygon inside the cell. Size the SVG at min(560px, 60vh). Make vertices draggable via pointer events on the <circle>s, with 0.1 mm snapping to cell edges and existing vertices. Show live edge-length labels and the closing segment. Highlight invalid pieces (see the structured-errors finding). Keep validateFreePieces as the single source of truth so no wrong dimensions are ever shown.
corrected:
Problem: confirmed. Proposal: changed in a few places. All changes are in FreeformEditor (src/ui/project/StoneDialog.tsx). validateFreePieces and setFreePieces in src/core/edits.ts stay the only gate on what can be saved.

1. Drawing area
- Give the <svg> a viewBox in mm units, e.g. viewBox={`-pad -pad ${cellW+2pad} ${cellH+2pad}`}. Size it with CSS: width: min(560px, 100%), aspect-ratio matching the cell, max-height: 60vh.
- Convert pointer positions to mm with svg.getScreenCTM().inverse() instead of the fixed `s`/`pad` math at :324-330. Otherwise clicks land in the wrong place whenever CSS max-width shrinks the SVG.

2. Vertex dragging
- Add onPointerDown with setPointerCapture and stopPropagation on each <circle>, then update the point via setPt on pointermove. Make the hit radius larger (r of about 8 px, transparent).
- Add points on pointerup only when the pointer moved less than about 3 px and the press did not start on a vertex. This fixes the bug where a drag adds a stray point (repro: the drag added point (1.4, 1.4)).
- Snap to 0.1 mm and to cell edges and existing vertices within about 0.2 mm.
- Add a 'Punkt löschen' control on each vertex row of the table.

3. Starting empty and presets
- Add a 'Leeren / Neu zeichnen' button that sets pieces to [{poly: [], color: current}]. Keep the current pre-fill so existing shapes can still be edited.
- Add presets (Dreieck, Trapez, Raute, Rechteck) that create a single piece inside the cell. If a preset creates more than one piece, separate the pieces by layout.joint, the same way diagA/diagB in src/core/pieces.ts do.
- When '+ Neues Teil' is pressed while the existing pieces already cover nearly the whole cell, show a hint to shrink or delete them first.

4. Live measurements
- While drawing, show the length of each edge (Math.hypot of consecutive vertices, n(…,1) mm) and the dashed closing segment. Show the piece's area in the side panel. These values come only from the drawn coordinates; nothing is estimated.

5. Errors
- Translate the validator codes ('overlap i/j', 'piece n: self-intersecting/outside/area/<3') through i18n keys in de/en/tr.
- Outline the pieces involved in a dashed red stroke.
- Speichern stays disabled whenever v.ok is false.

Improve FreeformEditor (src/ui/project/StoneDialog.tsx:311-453) and keep all geometry in pure core functions with tests.

1. Pass the joint to the editor. Add `joint={layout.joint}` to FreeformEditor and add `joint: number` to its props.

2. Joint check in core. Add `minPolyDistance(a, b)` to src/core/geometry.ts (the minimum distance between the edges of two polygons). In validateFreePieces, add an optional `joint` parameter. When two pieces are closer than `joint - 0.05` mm, push a warning such as `gap i/j < joint`, shown as "Fuge zwischen Teil 1 und 2 nur 0,0 mm (Projekt: 1,5 mm)". Use a warning, not an error, so existing saved projects still open. Add vitest cases: 0 mm, 0.5 mm and 1.5 mm gaps against a 1.5 mm joint.

3. Toolbar.
   - 'Neu zeichnen' resets to `[{ poly: [], color: current }]` with active = 0.
   - Presets come from a new pure function `freePreset(kind, w, h, joint)` in src/core/pieces.ts, built on diagA/diagB/lineSplit/subRects (all joint-aware).
   - Preset kinds: Ganzer Stein, Diagonal ╲, Diagonal ╱, Halbiert, Raute (cell-midpoint rhombus), Trapez.
   - Do not round preset or initial vertices to 0.1 mm. Line 321 currently does, which can shrink the joint. Round only points the user clicks or drags.
   - Unit-test that every preset passes validateFreePieces with no gap warning.
   - Add one line to the free.hint text: "Bestehende Teile sind vorgeladen – 'Neu zeichnen' für leere Zelle."

4. Responsive canvas.
   - Give the SVG `viewBox="0 0 W H"` with `width: 100%; max-height: 60vh`, keeping the cell's aspect ratio.
   - Convert pointer positions with `svg.getScreenCTM().inverse()` instead of the fixed `pad`/`s` pixel math.
   - Scale the 1 mm grid lines and vertex radius to the viewBox.

5. Draggable vertices.
   - Circles: onPointerDown calls stopPropagation and setPointerCapture. onPointerMove calls setPt with round1 and clamps to [0, cellW] x [0, cellH]. Snap to cell edges within 0.2 mm.
   - Do NOT snap to other pieces' vertices. If any snapping is offered, snap to a point offset by `joint` from the neighbouring edge.
   - Set `touch-action: none` on the SVG so the page does not scroll while dragging on Android.
   - Ignore the click that follows a drag so no extra point is added.
   - Optional: click an edge midpoint to insert a vertex; long-press or right-click a vertex to delete it.

6. Live measurements, computed only from the drawn coordinates (exact, nothing estimated).
   - Edge lengths at each edge midpoint (mm, 1 decimal), with the closing segment drawn dashed.
   - Bounding box w×h and area for the active piece.
   - Label these clearly as the drawn contour. After saving, the cut template (CutTemplateSvg / cutInfo) stays the authoritative output.

7. Errors. Draw pieces with errors or warnings in red (self-intersecting, outside, overlap, too thin, gap below joint). Localize the raw error codes ('overlap 1/3', 'piece 1: <3') via i18n (de/en/tr), together with the structured-errors finding.

8. E2E. Open freeform on a diagonal cell, press 'Neu zeichnen', draw a triangle, drag one vertex and check that its coordinates in the table changed. Save, then check that stone counts and the cut template reflect the new piece.

findings.title: Material links are lost on project export/import, and deleting a used material silently changes the material calculation
findings.problem: exportProject writes only record, image, mosaic and progress. The materials referenced by palette[i].materialId and settings.materialIds are not included. After importing on a second device (the README recommends this for PC↔tablet), every material link is dangling. The stone detail shows 'Material: ?', raw-stone counts fall back to the grid size, and pack and cost information disappears. None of this is flagged. The same happens on the same device when a used material is deleted: Materials.tsx only asks 'Material löschen?'. Material DB edits (hex, size) and new materials (materialIds=[] means 'all') also never mark a materials-mode project as stale. A second minor point: an import gets exactly the same name as the existing project.
findings.evidence: Repro: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/correctness-ui-state/t9_materials_export_import.cjs plus mats.csv, output t9_output.txt. Device 1: 'Material: Bisazza Vetricolor 09', 'Rohsteine inkl. Reserve 1.982', 'Kosten 0,55'. 'export contains materials? false | palette entries with materialId: 10 / 10'. After deleting 6 materials on device 1: 'stale badge = false', 'Rohsteine inkl. Reserve 3.387', 'Kosten 0,25 unvollständig'. Device 2 after import: 'Material: ?', 'Rohsteine inkl. Reserve 6.367', no cost row (screenshot t9-device2-matcalc.png). Code: projects.ts:208-226 (payload without materials), Materials.tsx:188-191 (delete with no usage check), useProject.ts:27 (key uses only materialIds).
findings.proposal: (1) Export: add `materials: Material[]` holding every material referenced by the palette or settings.materialIds. Import: upsert them by id, or match an existing material by manufacturer+colorNumber+hex. Report 'X Materialien übernommen, Y zugeordnet'. Append ' (Import)' to the imported project's name. (2) On delete in Materials, scan listProjects() for references and show 'Wird in Projekt A, B verwendet – Materialbedarf ändert sich'. (3) In PaletteEditor and StoneDialog, show a warning badge 'Material fehlt' when materialId is set but not found, instead of '?'. In MaterialCalc, list colours whose raw size fell back to the grid size. (4) For materials and auto-snap modes, add a fingerprint of the used materials (id+hex+size) to computeKey.
corrected:
(1) Export: in src/storage/projects.ts exportProject, add `materials: Material[]` to the payload. Include every material whose id appears in record.palette[].materialId or settings.materialIds; when materialIds is [] ('all'), include only the palette-referenced ones. Import, in importProject:
- For each exported material: if a local material with the same id exists, keep the local one and do not overwrite it.
- Otherwise, if a local material matches by manufacturer+product+colorNumber (trimmed, case-insensitive), map the old id to the local id.
- Otherwise, insert the exported material with its original id.
- Rewrite palette[].materialId and settings.materialIds through that mapping before saveProject.
- Return the counts and show 'X Materialien übernommen, Y zugeordnet' in Projects.tsx.
- Append ' (Import)' to meta.name when a project with the same name already exists.

(2) Material CSV (Materials.tsx materialsToCsv/parseMaterialsCsv): add an 'id' column. On CSV import, reuse the id if present and upsert by id; otherwise fall back to a manufacturer+product+colorNumber match before creating a new uid(). This lets the CSV route keep links intact.

(3) Delete: in the Materials.tsx delete handler, load the projects and count the ones whose palette or settings.materialIds reference m.id. If any do, the confirm text names them ('Wird in Projekt A, B verwendet – Materialbedarf/Kosten ändern sich').

(4) Missing-material visibility instead of silent fallback:
- In makeRawSizeFn, return a `missing: true` flag when materialId is set but not found. Collect these colours into a `missingMaterials: number[]` field on Stats and set costComplete=false for them.
- StoneDialog.tsx:129-131: show a warning badge 'Material fehlt (gelöscht oder nicht importiert)' instead of '?'.
- StepColors.tsx, material column: show the same badge.
- StepPlan.tsx material calc: list the affected colour codes with 'Rohsteinmaß = Rastermaß (Material fehlt)'. Render the cost row whenever any colour has a material reference, even if totalCost is 0, with the 'unvollständig' badge.
- PDF material list: same marking.

Do NOT add a material fingerprint to computeKey or otherwise mark the project stale. A recompute wipes manual edits and laying progress, and with materialIds=[] any new material would invalidate every materials-mode project. If desired, show a non-blocking info note ('Materialdaten seit der Berechnung geändert') that does not suggest recomputing.

(1) **Export/import (src/storage/projects.ts:75-118).**
- Raise the payload version to 2 and add `materials: Material[]`. Include only materials referenced by `palette[i].materialId`, plus the explicit `settings.materialIds` when that list is not empty. Do not export the whole catalog when the list is [] ('all').
- On import, handle each exported material in this order:
  - (a) If a local material with the same id exists, keep the local one. Never overwrite it. If its hex or size differs from the exported one, record that as a note.
  - (b) Otherwise, look for an exact match on normalised manufacturer + product + colorNumber + lengthMm × widthMm. If found, remap that id in the palette and in `settings.materialIds`.
  - (c) Otherwise, insert the exported material under its own id.
- Never pick a 'nearest' material automatically.
- Show a summary message: 'X Materialien neu angelegt, Y vorhandenen zugeordnet, Z mit abweichenden Daten'.
- For a version 1 file, warn: 'Datei enthält keine Materialien – N Farben ohne gültiges Material'.
- Append ' (Import)' to the imported project's name.
- Add an optional `id` column to the materials CSV (Materials.tsx:25) and reuse it on CSV import, so a CSV round trip keeps the links.

(2) **Delete in Materials.tsx:186-193.** Before calling confirm, run listProjects() (db.ts:91). Count the projects whose palette or settings.materialIds reference the material, and say so in the confirm text: 'Wird in Projekt A, B (n Farben) verwendet – Materialbedarf und Kosten dieser Farben werden danach ohne Material berechnet.' Optionally offer to replace it with another material before deleting.

(3) **Make the fallback visible.**

globalRules:
Implementation plan for making MosaicPlan "much, much better": 7 waves, 33 work packages, ordered by user impact. The order is: (1) data safety and geometric correctness; (2) workspace safety UI, Android platform, honest colours, honest preview, photo intake and design system; (3) mosaic colour quality, live preview, freeform editor, face/detail guidance, viewer features, PDF foundations and project portability; (4) cut placement and accent colours, laying workbench, progress engine, PDF sheet structure, offline face detector; (5) undo/redo, single-pass stats, viewer back-buffer, PDF content, shopping view, target colours, PDF export UI; (6) deviation map and batch editing, fine-tile materials, colour measuring, streaming CSV, final PDF wiring; (7) docs and e2e consolidation.

RULES FOR EVERY PACKAGE

Files and parallel work
- Packages in the same wave run in parallel. They own disjoint existing files.
- New files may be created freely, but each name must be unique to its package.
- Some packages add optional fields or parameters only so that a package in the next wave can compile. Each one is marked "contract for wave N". Add them exactly as written, even if nothing in your package uses them.

Translations (i18n)
- Put new keys in src/i18n/ext/<package-id>.ts and export {de, en, tr}. The aggregator in src/i18n/index.ts merges every ext file after the base dictionaries.
- All three languages must have the same keys and the same placeholders. tests/i18n.test.ts checks this.
- To change the wording of an existing key, override it in your own ext file. First grep src/i18n/ext to make sure no other ext file already overrides that key.
- Never edit de.ts, en.ts or tr.ts.

CSS
- Only w2-design-system edits src/ui/styles.css.
- Every other package puts its CSS in src/ui/css/<package-id>.css and imports it from a component it owns.

Tests
- Unit tests go in tests/<package-id>*.test.ts.
- Browser checks are standalone Playwright scripts at e2e/<package-id>.e2e.cjs, run against `npm run preview`.
- Only w7-docs-e2e touches e2e/run-e2e.cjs and README.md.
- The golden mosaic hash fixture is tests/golden/mosaic-hashes.json. It hashes kind, c1, c2, rec, sub, line, free and palette hex+code, but not names. It is owned by whichever package owns src/core/mosaic.ts in that wave. Any change to it must be deliberate and explained in the PR.

Quality bar
- Every package must leave `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build` and the existing `node e2e/run-e2e.cjs` green.
- Every package must keep the exact-geometry and count guarantees: totals equal the geometry, and cut dimensions come only from analyzeCut on real polygons.
- Anything estimated must be labelled 'Schätzung' or 'Richtwert'. Requirement 18 holds everywhere.
deferred: Grout compensation in computeMosaic (algo-quality#0, part 4). Both reviewers called it optional and off by default, and recommending a grout plus an honest preview gives most of the benefit. Changing the factory grout default from #BDB8AE to #808080 is deferred too; the recommendation never overwrites the user's choice.

Linear-light averaging of stone target colours (algo-quality#10). Measured gains are within k-means noise on natural photos. Revisit it together with linear-light resizing in imageOps, with a measured A/B benchmark.

Mixed tile sizes stage 2: zones with their own grid (spec-gaps#2). Wave 6 delivers stage 1, real fine-tile materials for k×k sub-stones plus fine regions. Zones touch every per-cell structure (progress mask, IDs, sections, hit-testing, PDF), and the tiles-step badge stays honest until then.

Movable section boundaries and a seam optimiser (spec-gaps#9). This is impact 2-3 and needs new settings across layout, viewer, worker and PDF. Paper-matched section presets (wave 6) cover the main paper-waste pain.
Full SVG export of plans and templates (spec-gaps#12). The vector PDF at 1:1 or custom paper already covers plotters. Only PNG preview export is built (wave 6).

Diff-based incremental statistics in a worker that keeps its own mosaic copy, and dirty-pixel overview updates (performance-scale#5, parts 2-3). They are replaced by the 8-13x single-pass stats (wave 5), coalesced stats jobs and O(1) progress counters (wave 4). Revisit only if 5M-stone edits are still slower than about 1 s.
Splitting the shape analysis across several workers (performance-scale#7, part b). The hot-loop fix gives about 4x. SharedArrayBuffer is not available without COOP/COEP headers.
One CSV per section, delivered as a ZIP (performance-scale#1). Streaming CSV plus the Excel row-limit warning are built; a store-only ZIP can follow if users ask.
Automatic stock-constrained recolouring (spec-gaps#4, part 4). It would change how the image looks and is often impossible. Exact shortfall and shopping lists are built instead.

Error-driven k-means swap refinement and detail-weighted palette samples (algo-quality#6, optional part). Measured gains were inconsistent. Pinned accent colours confirmed by the user are built instead.
Dither error diffusion through split/SUB cells, serpentine scanning and face/edge damping (algo-quality#1). Measured as useless or harmful.
Global cut budget, 'max. Schnittzellen' (algo-quality#3, phase 2). The background cut factor in wave 4 gives most of the value.
Image-level Canny/polyline contour extraction (algo-quality#5). Unproven, and it would defeat template reuse. Only the opt-in grid-preserving continuity bonus is built.
Haptic feedback with the VIBRATE permission (ux-mobile-android#2). The text status line and flash highlight already give feedback.
A native 'pause' flush registry through @capacitor/app (ux-mobile-android#1). beforeunload with commit(), visibilitychange and minimizeApp already cover saving.
MediaPipe face detection. Its 14.6 MB wasm exceeds the PWA precache limit; pico.js is used instead (wave 4).
Colour-chart sheet mode for measuring many tiles from one photo (spec-gaps#7, phase 2).
First-fit-decreasing packing of mixed-width strips into shared raw tiles (correctness-core#5, optional). The current per-shape-group count is a safe upper bound.
Mixed page orientations per section and tighter print margins (pdf-print#4). Mixed orientations risk print-dialog auto-scaling, which breaks 1:1. Smaller margins clip on common printers.
Undo history that persists across reloads (ux-desktop#7). The journal is in memory for the session only, and the README will say so.
